findings.reason: validateSkillset (fetch-skillset.ts:12) only checks that name is a string. install.ts:121 joins it into tmpDir, so '../../home/alice' becomes /home/alice. safePath only checks against that already-escaped base, and a source of '.' gets past the '..' check in resolve-skillset.ts:33. The result is writeFile to an attacker-chosen path.
findings.claim: A manifest name containing ../ moves the download directory outside tmpdir/spm, so remote content can overwrite user files.
findings.evidence: validateSkillset only checks that name is a string. With tmpdir()='/tmp', name='../../home/alice', source='.' and files=['.bashrc'], join constructs '/home/alice', safePath accepts '/home/alice/.bashrc', and writeFile overwrites it with downloaded content. An in-memory execution recorded that destination.

findings.reason: The '@' branch in resolve-skillset.ts:17-28 never rejects '..', so the path becomes '../demo-evil/payload.md'. resolve gives /tmp/spm/demo-evil/..., which still passes startsWith('/tmp/spm/demo') at install.ts:85. Lowered to medium because the write stays inside tmpdir/spm, in a sibling skillset directory.
findings.claim: The startsWith containment check lets '@org/repo/../sibling' sources write into sibling skillset directories.
findings.evidence: With name='demo', source='@org/repo/../demo-evil' and files=['payload.md'], resolveSkillset emits '../demo-evil/payload.md'. safePath('/tmp/spm/demo', ...) accepts '/tmp/spm/demo-evil/payload.md' because startsWith(baseDir) is true. The raw GitHub URL normalizes to the demo-evil branch, so a repository containing that branch and file can supply the payload. An in-memory execution recorded the sibling write destination.

findings.reason: The regex at parse-identifier.ts uses a non-capturing tree/[^/]+ segment, and the returned identifier has no ref. resolve-identifier.ts:20 then always calls fetchDefaultBranch. The new test even asserts that a 'develop' URL gives no branch, so the content installed comes from another branch.
findings.claim: GitHub tree URLs drop the branch, so install fetches the default branch instead.
findings.evidence: For 'https://github.com/org/repo/tree/develop/pkg', parseGitHubUrl returns only owner, repository and path. resolveIdentifier then fetches the repository's default branch. With default_branch='main', an in-memory execution requested '/org/repo/main/pkg/skillset.yml' and downloaded files from main despite the explicit develop URL.

members.claim: GitHub URLs discard their requested branch, causing installation of different content or a download failure.

findings.reason: downloadEntries passes location.ref to every entry at install.ts:71, including '@other/repo' entries that resolve-skillset.ts:24-28 points at another repo, and no branch lookup is done for them. Lowered to medium because a mismatch fails loudly (404 rejects Promise.all) rather than corrupting anything.
findings.claim: Cross-repo skill entries are downloaded using the manifest repo's ref.
findings.evidence: downloadEntries passes location.ref to every toGitHubSource call, including entries whose owner and repository differ. If the manifest repository defaults to main and '@other/legacy/skills/example' exists only on master, the downloader requests '/other/legacy/main/skills/example/SKILL.md'; its 404 rejects Promise.all and aborts installation before writing files. No branch lookup is performed for other/legacy.

findings.reason: install.ts:75 sets path to entry.path, and line 128 builds the destination from that path alone, without owner or repository. Two cross-repo sources with the same path therefore race on writeFile in Promise.all.
findings.claim: Files from different repos with the same repo-relative path collide on one destination.
findings.evidence: Two skills sourced from '@one/repo/skills/example' and '@two/repo/skills/example', each listing 'SKILL.md', both reach writeFile at '/tmp/spm/demo/skills/example/SKILL.md'. The destination uses result.path without owner or repository, and Promise.all writes both concurrently. An in-memory execution recorded both different contents targeting that same file.

findings.reason: 'test-skillset' has no @ and isn't a URL, so parseIdentifier throws after info('Resolving ...') has already printed (install.ts:104-105). The test only checks stdout and ignores the exit code and stderr.
findings.claim: The install integration test passes even when install fails, so the download and write path is never checked.
findings.evidence: The test runs 'install test-skillset' and asserts only that stdout contains 'Resolving test-skillset'. That message is printed before parseIdentifier rejects the unsupported bare identifier; the catch sets exitCode=1. An in-memory execution produced the expected message with exitCode=1, zero fetches and zero writes, while the test ignores both code and stderr.

findings.reason: README.md:20 shows a bare name, which parseIdentifier now rejects. install.ts:121 writes under tmpdir()/spm, not into the project. This is a stale-documentation point, so it stays low.
findings.claim: The README's 'spm install nextjs-fsd' example no longer works, and files land in tmpdir rather than the project.
findings.evidence: README recommends 'spm install nextjs-fsd' and says it installs into the project. The new install action passes that bare name directly to resolveIdentifier, whose parser accepts only @ identifiers or GitHub URLs. Successful downloads are written under tmpdir()/spm rather than into the project.
